messages:
olivia: Heads-up - onboarding Tethys-14B int4 we saw intermittent tail-latency spikes at ~95th-99th pct for streaming responses starting at ~concurrency 8. Not OOMs, just long stalls (~700-1200ms extra). Any ideas?
raj: Can you paste the perf logs and the config you used for the canary?
olivia: sure - running canary on dedicated pool, 8xA10g, batch.window_ms=18, batch.max_batch_tokens=4096, kernel_mode=auto, quant=ptq-int4. Logs: ``
[2026-02-10 14:12:33] request=abc123 latency=89ms tokens=42
[2026-02-10 14:12:34] request=def456 latency=1280ms tokens=41  <-- stall during kv fetch
[2026-02-10 14:12:34] request=ghi789 latency=95ms tokens=3
```
cheng: Hm looks like occasional kernel recompile/selection or cache miss in the tiled-attn path. We've seen int4 + short windows cause the runtime to switch kernel plans mid-request. Does runtime trace show kernel_pick events?
olivia: yes, infra-bot posted trace earlier but here's the relevant snippet: ``kernel_pick: plan=v2_tiled_unfused (switch from v1) at step=6, reason=seq_len>32 && requested_kv_prefetch=on``
raj: That explains it. When plan flips it flushes some internal buffer and that introduces a stall. Two immediate levers: 1) force stable kernel plan for this model by setting kernel_mode=prefer_stable, 2) widen batching window to avoid borderline seq_len decisions (try 30ms).
sara: Also saw a small quality delta on instruction-following after PTQ-int4 - around 2-3% avg BLEU drop on our eval set. Not huge but visible. We should gate by eval before flipping defaults.
olivia: Ran quick A/B after forcing kernel_mode=prefer_stable + batch.window_ms=30: P95 tail spikes disappeared in the canary (max extra stall ~120ms). Perf numbers: baseline canary (auto): P50=78ms P95=540ms P99=1200ms; stable plan: P50=82ms P95=150ms P99=260ms.
raj: Nice. Any memory overhead from prefer_stable?
olivia: small, ~60MB per worker due to keeping alternate kernels resident. Acceptable for Dedicated but might matter on Private small clusters.
cheng: For quality regression: can we run qeval on the same prompt set but enable mixed fallback: if logprob drop > threshold, fallback to fp16 execution for that request? We have runtime flags for dynamic_fallback=true + fallback_threshold=1.25 (relative perplexity).
sara: That would keep perf for the normal cases and avoid visible regressions. But we need to track cost delta. Add cost telemetry flagged in the rollout.
olivia: Proposal: for Tethys-14B int4 onboard rollout -> set defaults: kernel_mode=prefer_stable, batch.window_ms=30, dynamic_fallback=true, fallback_threshold=1.25, keep quant=ptq-int4. Start with 10% canary for 24h, monitor P95 latency and eval pass-rate. If eval pass-rate < 98% revert quant path.
raj: +1. Also add an aggressive kernel warmup on instance start to prepopulate tiled-attn kernels: warmup_sequence=["Hello", "Summarize:", "Translate:"] x2. That seems to reduce first-minute tail spikes.
infra-bot: deploy plan created: canary/tethys-int4-stable-20260210 by olivia. Rollout: 10% -> 24h -> metrics() -> auto-hold if P95 > 300ms or eval_pass_rate < 98%.
cheng: I'll open a tiny runtime patch to make kernel picks deterministic under prefer_stable - avoids future surprises. Will link PR.
olivia: Linking quick runbook for oncall: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/tethys-int4-onboard. Steps to rollback included.
sara: I'll run full eval overnight and post numbers in morning. If quality looks fine we can increase to 50% next day.
raj: Thanks all. Quick note: avoid changing batch.max_batch_tokens for now - that affects memory fragmentation patterns. Let's iterate on window_ms and kernel_mode first.
olivia: Agreed. Will push the canary config now and tag the thread with results tomorrow. :thumbsup:
